ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The discrete-time signal x[n] in the attached figure has only four nonzero samples, with vertical lines of height 1 drawn at n=0,1,2,3 respectively; other sampling positions are on the horizontal axis, represented as 0. Reasoning: Therefore x[n]=1 holds only for n=0,1,2,3. According to the DTFT definition, X(Ω)=Σ_{n=-∞}^{∞}x[n]e^{-jΩn}=Σ_{n=0}^{3}e^{-jΩn}=1+e^{-jΩ}+e^{-j2Ω}+e^{-j3Ω}. This is a finite geometric sum, with common ratio e^{-jΩ}, so X(Ω)=(1-e^{-j4Ω})/(1-e^{-jΩ}). Comparing with the given form X(Ω)=(1-e^{-jaΩ})/(1-e^{-jΩ}), obtain a=4.
